pages.text: On Saturday morning, eight-year-old Kofi held up a shiny one-cedi coin he had saved from helping sweep the compound. ‘Maame!’ he called excitedly. ‘I want to start a business today with my one cedi!’ Maame smiled over her sewing table. ‘One cedi is a wonderful seed, Kofi, but let us check what materials actually cost before you begin.’
sentences: On Saturday morning, eight-year-old Kofi held up a shiny one-cedi coin he had saved from helping sweep the compound.
‘Maame!’ he called excitedly.
‘I want to start a business today with my one cedi!’ Maame smiled over her sewing table.
‘One cedi is a wonderful seed, Kofi, but let us check what materials actually cost before you begin.’
pages.alt: Eight-year-old Kofi holds up a shiny one-cedi coin beside his mother Maame at her neat sewing and craft table.

pages.text: First, Maame taught Kofi the most important rule of enterprise: look for a real problem people want solved. At the Saturday reading club, Kofi noticed that children kept losing their page in their storybooks and folding down the corners of the paper! ‘If we make strong, colourful corner bookmarks that slip right over the page,’ said his sister Ama, ‘readers will never lose their place!’
sentences: First, Maame taught Kofi the most important rule of enterprise: look for a real problem people want solved.
At the Saturday reading club, Kofi noticed that children kept losing their page in their storybooks and folding down the corners of the paper!
‘If we make strong, colourful corner bookmarks that slip right over the page,’ said his sister Ama, ‘readers will never lose their place!’
pages.alt: At a neighbourhood reading table, Kofi and Ama notice classmates losing their page and bending book corners.

pages.text: They checked the cost of supplies at the stationery kiosk. A pack of stiff coloured manila cards and a small tube of paper glue cost five cedis in total, enough to make ten neat bookmarks. Kofi looked at his single coin. ‘You cannot start most businesses with just one cedi alone,’ he realised. ‘One cedi is not enough for the card and glue!’
sentences: They checked the cost of supplies at the stationery kiosk.

Kofi looked at his single coin.
‘You cannot start most businesses with just one cedi alone,’ he realised.
‘One cedi is not enough for the card and glue!’
pages.alt: At a small stationery kiosk, Kofi looks at his single coin while Ama and Yaw inspect packs of coloured manila card and glue.

pages.text: ‘What if we pool our savings as partners?’ suggested Ama. Kofi put in his one cedi, Ama added two cedis from her savings box, and their cousin Yaw added two cedis. One cedi plus two cedis plus two cedis equalled five cedis of startup capital! Together, the three partners bought the coloured card and glue.
sentences: ‘What if we pool our savings as partners?’ suggested Ama.
Kofi put in his one cedi, Ama added two cedis from her savings box, and their cousin Yaw added two cedis.
One cedi plus two cedis plus two cedis equalled five cedis of startup capital!
Together, the three partners bought the coloured card and glue.
pages.alt: Kofi, Ama and Yaw place their coins together on the table to make five cedis of startup capital.

pages.text: On the veranda table, the three partners set up a tidy production line. Yaw measured and folded the stiff card into neat triangular pockets, Ama trimmed the edges smoothly, and Kofi decorated each bookmark with cheerful geometric patterns and animal faces. By afternoon, ten sturdy bookmarks stood in a bright row.
sentences: On the veranda table, the three partners set up a tidy production line.
Yaw measured and folded the stiff card into neat triangular pockets, Ama trimmed the edges smoothly, and Kofi decorated each bookmark with cheerful geometric patterns and animal faces.
By afternoon, ten sturdy bookmarks stood in a bright row.
pages.alt: Yaw folds card triangles, Ama trims them neatly, and Kofi draws cheerful animal faces to make ten colourful corner bookmarks.

pages.text: Now came a big decision: how much should one bookmark cost? Since they spent five cedis to make ten bookmarks, each bookmark cost fifty pesewas in materials. ‘If we sell each bookmark for one cedi,’ said Kofi, ‘it is affordable for our friends, and it covers our fifty-pesewa cost plus fifty pesewas for our hard work!’ They named it Kofi’s One-Cedi Bookmark Business.
sentences: Now came a big decision: how much should one bookmark cost?

‘If we sell each bookmark for one cedi,’ said Kofi, ‘it is affordable for our friends, and it covers our fifty-pesewa cost plus fifty pesewas for our hard work!’ They named it Kofi’s One-Cedi Bookmark Business.
pages.alt: Kofi shows a bookmark slipped neatly onto the corner of a storybook page while Ama and Yaw count out ten bookmarks.

pages.text: After reading club, children and parents gathered around their small table. One bookmark slipped onto a textbook corner without falling out! One by one, ten customers each paid one cedi for a bookmark. When the last bookmark was sold, Kofi counted the coins in their cash dish: ten times one cedi equalled ten cedis of total sales, called revenue!
sentences: After reading club, children and parents gathered around their small table.

One by one, ten customers each paid one cedi for a bookmark.
When the last bookmark was sold, Kofi counted the coins in their cash dish: ten times one cedi equalled ten cedis of total sales, called revenue!
pages.alt: Happy children and a parent buy the colourful corner bookmarks at the reading club while Kofi counts ten one-cedi coins.

pages.text: ‘We have ten cedis! Are we ten cedis richer?’ asked Yaw excitedly. ‘Wait!’ said Maame, opening a small notebook. ‘First you must subtract the five cedis of capital you spent on materials. Ten cedis of revenue minus five cedis of cost leaves five cedis of profit! Profit is what remains after every cost is paid.’
sentences: ‘We have ten cedis!
Are we ten cedis richer?’ asked Yaw excitedly.
‘Wait!’ said Maame, opening a small notebook.
‘First you must subtract the five cedis of capital you spent on materials.
Ten cedis of revenue minus five cedis of cost leaves five cedis of profit!
Profit is what remains after every cost is paid.’
pages.alt: Maame helps Kofi, Ama and Yaw separate the ten coins into two equal piles of five coins: five cedis to replace their capital and five cedis of profit.

pages.text: The three partners returned their original five cedis to their capital pouch so they could buy fresh card for next Saturday, and shared the five cedis of profit fairly according to what each partner contributed and worked on. Kofi smiled at his coin. One cedi alone could not buy everything, but with planning, teamwork and honest value, it had sparked a real business!

activities.question: Why did Kofi team up with Ama and Yaw before buying the materials?
options: Materials cost 5 cedis, so they pooled 1 + 2 + 2 cedis of capital
The stationery shop only sold card to three children at once
Kofi lost his one-cedi coin on the way to the kiosk
activities.explanation: One cedi alone was not enough for the 5-cedi materials, so pooling 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 cedis gave them the startup capital they needed.

activities.definition: The total money received from selling goods or services
distractors: The glue used to stick paper corners together
The money left over after subtracting costs

activities.question: When the children collected 10 cedis in revenue after spending 5 cedis on materials, what was their profit?
options: 5 cedis (10 cedis revenue minus 5 cedis cost)
10 cedis (all the coins in the bowl)
activities.explanation: Profit = Revenue (10 cedis) − Cost (5 cedis) = 5 cedis.

activities.prompt: Put the steps of Kofi’s business in the right order.
items: Notice that readers need bookmarks and pool 5 cedis of startup capital.
Make 10 sturdy bookmarks and sell them for 1 cedi each (10 cedis revenue).
Subtract the 5-cedi material cost from 10 cedis to find the 5-cedi profit.

activities.prompt: How did working fairly with Ama and Yaw help Kofi turn a tiny idea into something real?

glossary.definition: Money saved or pooled together to buy the materials needed to start a business
People who join their money, skills and work together to run a business and share the results fairly
The total money a business brings in from selling its goods or services before subtracting any costs
The money left over after subtracting all business costs from total revenue
